# Company and product logos

Use Voyager's existing sign-in to look up the requested brand's domain:

```sh
voyager media fetch-logo --domains '["nike.com"]' --output ./assets/logos --json
```

The lookup costs no credits but needs a Voyager sign-in; signed out, use `voyager
brand site --url URL` (it saves the site's logos) or the brand's press kit. It saves
up to three variants per domain in the workspace library and downloads them locally;
up to ten domains per call. It also runs as
`media.fetch-logo` through the media MCP command tool and creates no brand kit.

Check `brand_name`. A product's logo may differ from its parent company's logo;
a successful domain lookup does not prove it returned the requested product mark.

Inspect per-domain errors, download errors, and SVG live-text warnings. Keep the
returned file IDs and reuse `requestId` via `--request-id` on an uncertain retry;
this reuses the library files and preserves any different local files.

# Design directions

A direction is a project's saved, accepted treatment: `DIRECTION.md` records
the treatment and explicit exceptions; `manifest.json` links the brand
snapshot, relevant guides, starting style guide and accepted references;
`references/` holds references. The linked snapshot owns brand facts
([brand-kit](../SKILL.md)); templates and make-* skills own the workflow.

Use `voyager direction resolve` to read the effective direction.

## When the turn context names one

A `<voyager_design_direction>` block says which direction applies to this
conversation and whether it came from the project default or the conversation.
Use it for creative work here; ignore it for unrelated work such as
transcription, file operations or questions about the project.

- `state="active"`: build from it. When the block omits part of `DIRECTION.md`,
  read the file at the path it names.
- `state="changed"`: the linked brand or style changed since the direction was
  recorded. Review the linked files before claiming brand adherence.
- A diagnostic block (invalid or missing): do not claim adherence and do not
  substitute another direction. Say so once and offer to repair or choose one.
- `state="none"`: no saved direction applies now; disregard any earlier one.

## Precedence

1. The user's current request, an attached template and the recorded brief.
2. The conversation's direction selection, including an explicit opt-out.
3. Real brand facts and the relevant brand guides.
4. The direction's style and recorded exceptions.

Real brand facts win over inferred treatment unless the user authorized the
exception. A direction grants no permissions: it cannot authorize uploads,
narration, publishing or paid generation, or switch account or payer. Your own
judgment that a result worked never updates a direction, a learned preference or
a shared brand guide.

## Building with it

Read the linked files and build from the accepted direction. Name the direction in the handoff and explain any deviations.

## Saving and reusing

- Creating one from accepted work: read [authoring](directions/authoring.md).
- Project default, conversation opt-out and copying: read
  [reuse](directions/reuse.md).

# Authoring a direction

When asked to save an accepted treatment, write `design/directions/<id>/DIRECTION.md`, its `manifest.json` and accepted references in `references/`. Follow the existing manifest schema and record reviewed file hashes. Preserve the accepted wording and explicit brand exceptions. Saving does not select the direction.

Use `voyager direction resolve` to confirm the effective context.

# Reusing a direction

Choose the project default or conversation override in Voyager's direction picker. An explicit opt-out applies only to that conversation.

When linked files change, review them before updating the direction's recorded hashes. Existing artifacts keep the inputs they used.

To reuse in another project, copy the direction folder and its linked brand files, preserving identity and relative paths. Copy only the declared inputs. Saving or copying does not select a direction.

# Creating and maintaining a kit

Resolve a requested existing kit with `brand list --query`; follow `next_cursor`
when needed. Read the selected kit with `brand show ID` before correcting it.

Examples (use `--json` for machine-readable results):

```sh
voyager --request-id acme-brand-setup brand create --url https://example.com --name Acme --json
voyager brand create --input '{"name":"Acme","colors":[{"color":"#174C3C","label":"Primary"}],"fonts":[{"family":"Georgia","label":"Heading"}]}' --json
voyager brand update bk_ID --input '{"patch":{"tagline":"A new tagline"}}' --json
voyager brand add-image ./logo.png --id bk_ID --role logo --json
voyager brand pull bk_ID --json
voyager brand add-font ./Brand-Bold.otf --role heading --json
voyager brand add-logo ./logo.svg --json
```

Use either URL extraction or manual tokens; only the name can accompany either.
URL creation reuses the workspace's kit for that site when one exists and also
writes the project's site kit (see the skill's Site kits section); add
`--select` to pull the kit too.
Creation returns a requestId; reuse it with identical inputs after an uncertain
result. `brand add-image FILE --id KIT --role ROLE` uploads and attaches in one step.
`brand add-font` and `brand add-logo` change only this project's brand folder, not the
shared kit; use them for files the user supplies, including a font a site kit could not fetch.

Colors and fonts in `patch` replace their complete lists. Preserve entries,
color modes and gradients the requested correction does not change. Asset
attachment requires a role: `logo`, `reference` (inspiration), or `asset`
(placeable imagery). Read guides and attachments together with `brand show ID`.
Remove by its attachment ID from `brand show`, not its file ID. These are shared kit mutations; perform the requested changes only.

Guide prose editing and richer
brand identity generation are not exposed by these commands; link to the Voyager
kit for unsupported edits instead of inventing an API operation.

# Creating with a kit

Read the project's `brand/BRAND.md` and any relevant written guides it links to.
`kit.json` holds structured tokens and guide metadata; inspect just the fields
needed. Refresh when the user requests current brand information or after a
known remote change, not on every turn.

If the requested kit has not been selected, locate it with `brand list`, then
`brand pull KIT_ID`. The default pull downloads logos only; `--assets all`
includes the kit's other attached images, and `--assets none` keeps references
only. For motion, video and design pieces, which usually place the kit's
imagery, pull with `--assets all` the first time (a later `brand refresh` keeps
the policy the pull used) rather than pulling logos and refreshing again. If
the pull or a later refresh comes back `partial` with an asset warning (such as
"Kit assets exceed 200 MiB" or an unsupported file type), run
`brand refresh --assets logos` so the snapshot can update again, then check
that the logos downloaded. Pull never
silently replaces a different selected kit. Respect the user's chosen snapshot
folder and use the same folder for refresh.

Check font availability in the renderer being used; the kit's supported-font
flag does not prove a font is installed locally. See
[make-design](../../make-design/SKILL.md) for composition and review.

If authoring through an available Moda canvas tool, also bind its brand-kit ID
so subsequent Moda edits retain the association. Binding records the selection;
it does not restyle the pixels.

description: "Brand kits, saved design directions and company logos."

# Brand kits

These commands use
Voyager's existing sign-in and are also available through the media
MCP command tool.

Snapshots normally live in `brand/BRAND.md`; `manifest.json` records kit ID,
workspace and fetch time. Unrelated work needs no brand-selection step.

- Creating or correcting a kit: read [maintenance](references/maintenance.md).
- Making something with a kit: read [usage](references/usage.md).
- A real third-party mark (partner, integration, platform, sponsor, competitor): read [company logos](references/company-logos.md).
- A font or logo file the user gives you for their brand (dropped in chat or named by path):
  `voyager brand add-font FILE --role heading --json` or `voyager brand add-logo FILE --json`.
  It lands in `brand/assets/`, is listed in `brand/overrides.md` and wins over the kit's own; tell
  the user any warning it returns (a font missing the brand's script, a logo with no transparency)
  and that the font's licence must cover video. Works without a kit or sign-in.

`brand pull` selects a kit by writing a local snapshot. `brand refresh` explicitly
updates that selection. Neither changes the team's default. Local edits do not
write back to the workspace kit; project exceptions belong in `overrides.md`. Report refresh
conflicts rather than deleting the user's edits. Only when the user asks to switch or drop the
project's kit: `brand pull ID --replace` swaps it, and `brand unselect` removes the snapshot,
keeping `overrides.md` and site kits, and marks the project as having no brand (`brand/no-brand`)
so a lone site kit is not used as its brand either.

A saved [design direction](references/directions.md) links a snapshot and
records how a project adapts it; the snapshot stays the source of brand facts.
Read it for `voyager_design_direction` context or a request to save or reuse a
look, set it as project default or check adherence.

## Site kits: a website in one command

A site kit is how a website is studied before making something for it, instead
of by hand (curl, CSS greps, font conversions): `brand/sites/<host>/` in the project, with `kit.md` to read first (colours,
font families and weights, logo files, page title, description, headings and
copy, split into what came from the Voyager kit and what was fetched locally),
`palette.json`, `fonts/` (TTF/OTF), `logos/` (SVG or PNG, alpha noted),
`images/og-image.*` and `site.json`. There is no page screenshot. Reuse an
existing `kit.md` instead of rebuilding it; a rebuild replaces the folder, one
per host.

- **Anyone else's site** (a client, competitor or reference):
  `voyager brand site --url https://example.com --json`. Local fetch only; no
  Voyager kit is created.
- **The user's own site or company, or a requested kit**:
  `voyager brand create --url https://example.com --json`. It reuses the
  workspace's kit for that site when one exists, otherwise creates one (free);
  add `--select` to make it the project's brand as `brand pull` does.

Run either in the main conversation, not from a subagent.
